content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Request and confirm a simple day and time. Model: “Could I have an appointment on Friday at eleven, please?” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use making an appointment clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Could I have an appointment on Friday at eleven, please?” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where making an appointment is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about making an appointment.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about making an appointment. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What day does the speaker request?

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Stress ap-POINT-ment and TUES-day. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about making an appointment.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using making an appointment; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise making an appointment?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Could I have an appointment on Friday at eleven, please?

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about making an appointment with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about making an appointment. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Could I have an appointment on Friday at eleven, please? Submit your draft first.
